authority: CEO R321 §P0; Article XXVIII (no semantic promotion), Article XXXI (corrections become permanent machine memory)

R320_result_preserved.claim: P-19 MECHANISM_VERIFIED through svMultiPhysics obstruction test
R320_result_preserved.evidence: Distributed (9/10 channels, 1 obstructed = 10% capacity loss): inlet 1.10 mmHg. Single (90% obstructed = 90% capacity loss): inlet 3.13 mmHg. Ratio 35%.

R321_correction.problem: The R320 comparison is NOT a controlled equal-obstruction experiment. The distributed system lost 10% of capacity (1 of 10 channels). The single system lost 90% of capacity (90% obstruction of 1 channel). These are DIFFERENT obstruction fractions. The distributed system wins partly because it retained more open conductance — not because the distributed architecture is inherently safer at matched obstruction levels.

correct_classification.EXTERNAL_SOLVER_OBSTRUCTION_CROSSCHECK: PASS — svMultiPhysics ran and produced physically meaningful results
correct_classification.DECISIVE_MECHANISM_COMPARISON: INCOMPLETE — obstruction fractions were not matched. The comparison confounds architecture effect with capacity-retention effect.

R321_correction.what_R320_actually_proved: The solver can model obstruction scenarios. The distributed system with 10% capacity loss has lower pressure than single with 90% capacity loss. This is trivially true (more open channels = more drainage) and does NOT prove the distributed ARCHITECTURE is superior to a single channel with equivalent capacity retention.
R321_correction.what_R320_did_NOT_prove: That distributed architecture is superior to single-channel at MATCHED obstruction fractions (e.g., 50% capacity loss in both configurations).

R321_action: Run matched-obstruction experiments (P1): 50%/50% and 90%/90% comparisons. Only if distributed wins at matched obstruction can we claim MECHANISM_VERIFIED.
permanent_memory: This correction is permanent. Future P-19 claims must reference this correction. The R320 result is NOT deleted — it is reclassified. Per Article XXXI: the lesson (match obstruction fractions in comparative experiments) becomes a machine rule for all future comparative tests.
machine_rule_added: COMPARATIVE_OBSTRUCTION_MATCHING: When comparing distributed vs single architectures, obstruction fractions MUST be matched. Distributed (k of N channels obstructed) must be compared against single (k/N fraction obstructed). Confounding architecture with capacity retention is forbidden.
